title: Synaptic gradients transform object location to action.
source_locator: Extended Data Fig. 1e,f (+ source data sheet Extended Data Fig. 1e); Fig. 1e,f (DNp05 pooled); Supplementary Table 1 (Fig. 1e: Empty vs. DNp05 ns, P = 0.626); Supplementary Table 2
quote: Only DNp04, DNp11 and combination line activation increased takeoff rates significantly compared to that of controls (Extended Data Fig. 1e,f and Supplementary Table 1)
mapping_basis: Paper calls SS02612 (VT047755-AD; VT003280-DBD) 'DNp05', a MANC type name, but driver_lines.csv maps the same AD/DBD pair SS02612 to DNp07 (Namiki 2018 supp. file 3; eLife.107450 Supp. Table 5); followed the paper's name, confidence lowered for the conflict.
stimulation: four 624-nm LEDs, total irradiance 500 W m-2 at the fly; 50-ms photostimulation; one stimulus per fly; in the dark
sensory_condition: unrestrained fly on 5 x 5 mm glass platform (FlyPEZ), dark, 850-nm IR, 6,000 fps side and bottom video
penetrance: takeoff 15/311 (4.8%) vs Empty 25/600 (4.2%), NS; pooled DNp05 postural shift (Delta T2 leg angle at 75 ms) ns vs Empty (P = 0.626)
n_flies_note: 311 flies for takeoff (ED Fig. 1e source data); postural-shift panels pool both DNp05 lines (Fig. 1e n = 253; Fig. 1f n = 262)
notes: Only takeoff and middle-leg (T2) posture were scored, within a 100-ms tracked window after a 50-ms pulse; the pooled DNp05 Delta[T2 leg angle] trace stays flat near 0 (Fig. 1f). No stepping or other leg movement is described. Legs coded no under the no-visible-effect convention, but a 100-ms window cannot show 3+ step cycles, so confidence is low. LINE-IDENTITY CONFLICT: the kit maps SS02612 to DNp07; if the kit is right, this record belongs to DNp07.
